title: A Current for the Horizon
premise: Zephyrine Underhill, a disgraced mountain guide living off the grid on a fog-bound coast, discovers a cave exposed by an unprecedented low tide, inside which lies the wreck of the Meridian Star—a salvage ship that sank carrying the ledgers proving who really caused the disaster that ruined his name. Racing a ruthless salvage fleet that has six tides to reach it first, Zephyrine must team up with the daughter of the man he was blamed for losing on the mountain. In the end he recovers the ledgers but must choose between clearing his own name and protecting the surviving families of the crew; he chooses them, trading his anonymity for justice that never touches him.
about_author: Gideon Brightwater is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent a decade charting tidal caves along the northern coast before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people the maps forgot.

chapters.title: The Lowest Tide in Living Memory
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Working as an anonymous boat-hand, he watches the sea pull back farther than any old-timer can recall, revealing a black cave mouth beneath the cliffs. Local legend says the cave 'charges admission.' He almost walks away—then recognizes the wreck timbers inside. Emotional beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Admission
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He enters the cave at night and finds the Meridian Star, intact, its hold sealed. Among the debris: a brass strongbox stamped with the survey company that destroyed him ten years ago. He takes nothing but a photograph—and is seen leaving by someone on the cliff road. Beat: hope curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Blacklisted
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Zephyrine's POV. Ten years earlier: the Kestrel Pass expedition, the storm, the client lost, and the inquiry that blamed him while the company's falsified logs went unquestioned. Two countries revoke his certification. Beat: the wound explained—the ledgers could rewrite all of it.

chapters.title: The Fleet Arrives
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Three salvage vessels anchor in the bay, flying the colors of Halloran Marine—the same company. Their chief, Dree Voss, posts a reward for information about 'unauthorized diving.' Zephyrine realizes his silhouette was recognized. Beat: hunted begins.

chapters.title: The Daughter of Kestrel Pass
chapters.summary: Isla's POV introduced. Isla Marchetti, daughter of the lost client, arrives in town asking questions about the cave. She has spent ten years pulling her father's records apart and suspects the truth. She and Zephyrine meet hostile, each blaming the other's story. Beat: collision of griefs.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Isla shows Zephyrine her father's tide tables: the cave will be accessible only six more times before spring tides seal it for months. The fleet has divers and permits; they have nothing but knowledge of the approach currents. Uneasy alliance formed. Beat: reluctant partnership.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Isla's POV. First joint dive attempt thwarted by fleet spotter boats. They hide in a sea stack while Voss's divers probe the outer cave. Isla reveals she knows Zephyrine was framed—her father's last letter names Halloran. Beat: trust tentatively extended.

chapters.title: The Informant
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A dockside boy offers to sell their plans to Voss; instead Zephyrine turns him, feeding false coordinates. But the boy's handler is the harbormaster, whose loyalty is already bought. Beat: small victory shadowed by betrayal.

chapters.title: Dead Reckoning
chapters.summary: Isla's POV. They plan a night run through the Serrated Reach, a current channel only Zephyrine can read. Tension between them: she wants the ledgers published, he wants them used quietly to protect the crew families still paid hush money. Beat: the moral fault line drawn.

chapters.title: Tide Three
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Second dive succeeds partially—they reach the strongbox but it's bolted to the captain's safe, which needs cutting gear they don't have. Inside the wreck, Zephyrine finds his own old guide rope, lost on Kestrel Pass, impossibly far from any mountain. Beat: the past made physical.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Dree Voss's POV. Her employer isn't Halloran Marine but its founder personally, dying and desperate to bury the ledgers. Voss, a salvager with her own code, grows uneasy about drowning two civilians for paper. Beat: antagonist humanized, stakes sharpened.

chapters.title: Storm Glass
chapters.summary: Isla's POV. Weather turns; a gale will make tides four and five undivable, collapsing their window to one. The harbormaster tips off Voss about the Serrated Reach route. Zephyrine decides they must go tonight, in the storm's leading edge. Beat: desperation becomes resolve.

chapters.title: The Serrated Reach
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The night run through the channel—white water, hidden teeth of rock, the boat nearly lost. Zephyrine's mountain instincts save them where charts fail. Isla sees for the first time the guide he might have been. Beat: earned awe, deepening bond.

chapters.title: Tide Five
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Inside the cave in rising water, they cut the safe free just as the fleet's second team breaks through the outer passage. A near-drowning; Isla saves Zephyrine from a collapsed beam. They surface outside with the safe—but Voss has their boat. Beat: triumph stolen.

chapters.title: Bargaining with the Sea
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Stranded on the cliffs, safe in hand but no way off, they open it: the ledgers, plus a confession letter naming Halloran's founder and the bribed inquiry officials. Also a list of crew families still receiving silence payments. Beat: the choice crystallizes.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Isla's POV. Argument at its sharpest: publication clears Zephyrine and ruins the families' income; silence protects them and leaves him condemned forever. Isla realizes her father would have chosen the families. Zephyrine, for once, argues for himself—and hates it. Beat: both characters broken open.

chapters.title: The Trap at Carrick Light
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Voss corners them at the lighthouse, offering passage in exchange for the ledgers. Zephyrine counters: he'll give her the confession letter to deliver to the maritime court himself—if she testifies. Voss's code wavers. Beat: the antagonist offered redemption.

chapters.title: Last Tide
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Final accessible tide: they return one last time—not for treasure but to recover the crew's personal effects, returning them to the families. The fleet watches, ordered to intervene, and Voss refuses the order. Beat: quiet defiance, the sea giving back what it took.

chapters.title: The Inquiry Reopened
chapters.summary: Isla's POV. Voss's testimony and the letter force a reopened inquiry. Zephyrine's name is cleared in absentia—but publishing the full ledgers would expose the hush payments. He asks Isla to hold them back. She agrees, keeping only her father's letter. Beat: sacrifice accepted.

chapters.title: A Current for the Horizon
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The founder's arrest makes national news; Zephyrine watches from a headland, unnamed in every report, exactly as he planned. Voss departs without a word but leaves him her tender. Beat: bittersweet vindication.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He takes work guiding again—informally, unlicensed, taking clients no one else will: the blacklisted, the broke, the blamed. Isla joins him for the first season. Beat: identity rebuilt on his own terms.

chapters.title: The Cave Keeps Its Admission
chapters.summary: Closing chapter, alternating brief POVs. Spring tides seal the cave for good. On the cliff above, Zephyrine and Isla leave flowers for the lost. The legend gets a new ending: the cave charged admission after all—ten years of a man's life. Beat: peace, memory honored, horizon open.
